topic: Extreme heat effects: skin blood flow, sweat rate, heatstroke threshold
hook: What extreme heat does to your body
tag_reason: Mayo Clinic is the source of the heatstroke definition (core temperature of 40°C / 104°F or higher)
caption:
In extreme heat, your body fights hard to stay near 37°C. It pushes blood toward your skin and pours out sweat, sometimes more than a liter an hour.

When that system can't keep up and your core reaches 40°C (104°F), doctors call it heatstroke. It is a medical emergency (source: Mayo Clinic).

Follow for one body fact a day that your brain won't believe. Which would you rather survive: extreme heat or extreme cold?
